text: Given more teams match name_prefix than page_size, When graph_list_teams is called, Then has_more is true and next_page_token equals the extracted $skiptoken from the fake Graph page's @odata.nextLink
Given the last page of teams (no @odata.nextLink in the fake Graph response), When graph_list_teams is called, Then has_more is false and next_page_token is null
Given a known test team's display-name prefix on the INT test tenant, When graph_list_teams(name_prefix=<prefix>) is called, Then teams[] contains that team's id and displayName
precond: needs a real vendor account: an MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant (per spec-check test note: e.g. the GDAP demo tenant 2qmxyw), a known test team whose displayName starts with an agreed prefix, and a valid X-Ms-Graph-Token for that tenant with Team.ReadBasic.All consented.
steps: Obtain a Graph access token for the INT test tenant (Team.ReadBasic.All consented).
Call graph_list_teams with name_prefix set to the known test team's agreed prefix via the MCP tool (initialize -> tools/call).
Read the JSON response.
expect: teams[] contains an entry whose id and displayName match the known test team; count >= 1.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given a known user_id who has joined a known test team on the INT test tenant, When graph_list_teams(user_id=<id>) is called, Then teams[] contains that team
precond: needs a real vendor account: same INT test tenant as TC-TEAMS-003, plus a known user's Entra object id or UPN who is a member of the known test team.
steps: Obtain a Graph access token for the INT test tenant (Team.ReadBasic.All consented).
Call graph_list_teams with user_id set to the known test user.
Read the JSON response.
expect: teams[] contains the known test team's id and displayName.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given a known team_id with a known test channel on the INT test tenant, When graph_list_channels(team_id) is called, Then channels[] contains that channel's id, membershipType and webUrl
precond: needs a real vendor account: same INT test tenant, the known test team's id, and a known test channel in it with Channel.ReadBasic.All consented.
steps: Obtain a Graph access token for the INT test tenant (Channel.ReadBasic.All consented).
Call graph_list_channels with team_id set to the known test team.
Read the JSON response.
expect: channels[] contains an entry whose id, membershipType and webUrl match the known test channel.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given the known test team has channels of more than one membershipType, When graph_list_channels(team_id, membership_type="standard") (and "private" if available) is called, Then every returned channel has exactly that membershipType
precond: needs a real vendor account: same as TC-TEAMS-005, plus at least one non-standard (private or shared) channel in the known test team.
steps: Call graph_list_channels(team_id=<known team>, membership_type="standard"); confirm every row has membershipType standard.
Call graph_list_channels(team_id=<known team>, membership_type="private") (if a private channel exists in the test team); confirm every row has membershipType private and no standard channel appears.
expect: Each call returns only channels of the requested membershipType; no cross-type leakage.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given a known channel with a configured email, When graph_get_channel(team_id, channel_id) is called, Then the response includes that channel's webUrl, isArchived and a non-empty email
precond: needs a real vendor account: same INT test tenant, a known channel in the known test team that has an email address configured (e.g. a standard channel, which Microsoft auto-provisions an email for).
steps: Call graph_get_channel(team_id=<known team>, channel_id=<known channel with email>).
Read the JSON response.
expect: Response has the channel's webUrl, isArchived (boolean), and a non-empty email string.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given a fake Graph channel payload with no email key, When graph_get_channel processes it, Then the tool's response has email as the explicit empty string "" and does not fail
Given a fake GraphClient that raises GraphError(403, ...) for /teams, When graph_list_teams is called, Then the error envelope names Team.ReadBasic.All, code is missing_scope, retryable is false

Given a fake GraphClient that raises GraphError(403, ...) for /teams/{id}/channels, When graph_list_channels is called, Then the error envelope names Channel.ReadBasic.All, code is missing_scope, retryable is false

Given a fake GraphClient that raises GraphError(403, ...) for /teams/{id}/channels/{id}, When graph_get_channel is called, Then the error envelope names the channel-read scope (Channel.ReadBasic.All or ChannelSettings.Read.All per the Open Questions resolution), code is missing_scope, retryable is false
Given a token from an INT test tenant that has not re-consented for the new scope, When any of the three tools is called, Then the response is the same named-scope error end to end, not a generic 500
precond: needs a real vendor account: an M365 tenant (or the same test tenant with the scope deliberately not yet granted) whose admin consent lacks Team.ReadBasic.All / Channel.ReadBasic.All -- per the spec-check's own test note, this may need an admin to set up (name the person if so).
steps: Obtain a Graph access token for a tenant/app registration that has NOT consented to the new scope.
Call graph_list_teams (or graph_list_channels / graph_get_channel).
Read the JSON response and the HTTP status.
expect: Response is a structured error naming the missing scope and stating an admin must re-consent; it is not an unhandled exception or a generic 500.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given the caller's token is issued for the INT test tenant, When any of the three tools is called, Then only that tenant's teams/channels are returned and no tool input accepts a different tenant id
precond: needs a real vendor account: the INT test tenant and its known team/channel.
steps: Inspect the three tools' input schemas (tools/list) and confirm none accepts a tenant_id or equivalent parameter.
Call graph_list_teams with the INT test tenant's token and confirm every returned team belongs to that tenant (cross-check a known team id from a different tenant is absent).
expect: No tenant-selecting parameter exists on any of the three tools; returned data is limited to the token's own tenant.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given the three tools are registered and deployed, When an admin opens this connector's per-tool authorization panel for an agent on INT, Then three new independent switches appear and turning them on enables no send tool
precond: needs a real vendor account: an MSPbots agent on INT with the Microsoft Graph connector attached, and the INT build containing this ticket's merge.
steps: Open the agent's Connectors section, expand the Microsoft Graph connector row.
Search the tool list for graph_list_teams, graph_list_channels, graph_get_channel.
Toggle them on and confirm the toast and the updated on-count.
Confirm no send/post-message tool appears in the same connector's tool list.
expect: All three tools appear with their own switch; toggling them on enables only reads, no send tool exists in this connector to enable.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (MSPbots test tenant with its own Microsoft 365 tenant) -- not available in this environment; not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md S2.5/S3.

text: Given the three tools are implemented, When the dev leg's [DEV] ticket comment is read back, Then it names the exact Graph permission each tool needs and states they are the least set that passes AC1-AC7
precond: none beyond the dev leg's own ticket comment.
steps: Read back the [DEV] comment posted on PRD-22034.

Confirm it names Team.ReadBasic.All (graph_list_teams) and Channel.ReadBasic.All (graph_list_channels, graph_get_channel; or ChannelSettings.Read.All if the Open Questions resolution required it) and states no broader scope was requested.
expect: The comment names the exact scopes and confirms they are least-sufficient.
evidence: [DEV] comment (posted via mbp.py exit, which reads it back) states the scopes used: Team.ReadBasic.All for graph_list_teams, Channel.ReadBasic.All for graph_list_channels and graph_get_channel, and that these are the least scopes that pass AC1-AC7 -- no broader scope was requested.
